en.B: I tell you, that night two people will be sleeping in one bed. One will be taken, and the other will be left behind.
en.R: I tell you, on that night two people will be asleep in the same bed. One of them will be taken. The other will be left.

es.L: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que en esa noche estarán dos en una cama; el uno será tomado y el otro será dejado.
es.B: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que esa noche dos personas estarán durmiendo en una misma cama. Una será llevada, y la otra será dejada atrás.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que esa noche dos personas estarán dormidas en la misma cama. Una de ellas será llevada. La otra será dejada.

sw.L: Nawaambia, usiku huo [watu] wawili watakuwa juu ya kitanda kimoja; mmoja atachukuliwa na yule mwingine ataachwa.
sw.B: Nawaambia, usiku huo watu wawili watakuwa wamelala kitanda kimoja. Mmoja atachukuliwa, na mwingine ataachwa nyuma.
sw.R: Nawaambia, usiku huo watu wawili watakuwa wamelala katika kitanda kimoja. Mmoja wao atachukuliwa. Mwingine ataachwa.

decisions.choice: taken ... left: one is taken to be with the Lord, the other left behind for judgment
alternatives: taken away in judgment, the other spared
decisions.reason: The words are not explained. "Taken" is used of receiving someone to be with oneself (John 14:3), which points to being gathered to the Lord. But in the flood and at Sodom (17:27, 29) people were taken away by judgment, and some read the picture that way. Either way, two people side by side meet different ends.

decisions.choice: in that night: at the time of the Son of Man's coming
decisions.reason: Jesus pictures people asleep at night and working by day (17:35); the coming may be at any hour.

decisions.choice: two: two people
decisions.reason: The Greek uses the masculine form for a pair, which may include a man and a woman.

decisions.choice: two people ... sleeping (B); asleep (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who is in the bed and what they are doing.

source.text: ἔσονται δύο ἀλήθουσαι ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό, ἡ μία παραλημφθήσεται ἡ δὲ ἑτέρα ἀφεθήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: There will be two grinding at the same [place], the one will be taken and the other will be left.

en.L: There will be two [women] grinding at the same [place]; the one will be taken and the other will be left."
en.B: Two women will be grinding grain together. One will be taken, and the other will be left behind."
en.R: Two women will be grinding grain together. One of them will be taken. The other will be left."

es.L: Dos [mujeres] estarán moliendo en el mismo [lugar]; una será tomada y la otra será dejada».
es.B: Dos mujeres estarán moliendo grano juntas. Una será llevada, y la otra será dejada atrás».
es.R: Dos mujeres estarán moliendo grano juntas. Una de ellas será llevada. La otra será dejada».

sw.L: [Wanawake] wawili watakuwa wakisaga mahali pamoja; mmoja atachukuliwa na yule mwingine ataachwa."
sw.B: Wanawake wawili watakuwa wakisaga nafaka pamoja. Mmoja atachukuliwa, na mwingine ataachwa nyuma."
sw.R: Wanawake wawili watakuwa wakisaga nafaka pamoja. Mmoja wao atachukuliwa. Mwingine ataachwa."

decisions.choice: two women grinding: two women working one hand mill together
decisions.reason: Grinding grain for the day's bread was women's work, often done by two women turning the upper stone of a hand mill together.

decisions.choice: no verse 36
alternatives: adding verse 36: two men will be in the field; one will be taken and the other left
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts, Codex Bezae among them, and some early translations add a verse like Matthew 24:40 about two men in a field. The oldest Greek manuscripts, including Papyrus 75, Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, do not have it, and it is probably copied from Matthew. The SBLGNT leaves it out, so there is no verse 36 here. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: grinding grain
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was ground.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here
decisions.reason: The disciples ask a question in 17:37.

decisions.choice: [Wanawake] (L); Wanawake (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek shows that the two are women only by the endings of its words (meaning decision m1). "Wawili" and "mmoja" do not show it in Swahili, so the word for women is supplied, in brackets at Literal, as in English.

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθέντες λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ποῦ, κύριε;

records.literal_gloss: And answering they say to him, Where, Lord?

en.L: And answering, they say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Where, Lord?"
en.B: They asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Where will this happen, Lord?"
en.R: The disciples asked, "Lord, where will this happen?"

es.L: Y respondiendo, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dicen: «¿Dónde, Señor?».
es.B: Ellos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron: «¿Dónde sucederá esto, Señor?».
es.R: Los discípulos preguntaron: «Señor, ¿dónde sucederá esto?».

sw.L: Nao wakijibu, wanamwambia, "Wapi, Bwana?"
sw.B: Walimwuliza, "Hayo yatatokea wapi, Bwana?"
sw.R: Wanafunzi walimwuliza, "Bwana, hayo yatatokea wapi?"

decisions.choice: where: where will these people be taken, or where will this happen
decisions.reason: The question is short and could ask either. Jesus' answer does not give a place.

decisions.choice: they say: a present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: Greek storytellers used the present tense to make a scene vivid.

decisions.choice: will this happen
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable complete the short question.

decisions.choice: asked
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the past tense of the story.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (le dicen); pretérito at Balanced and Readable (preguntaron)
decisions.reason: Luke tells this past event in the present (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Spanish narrative does.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (wanamwambia); past at Balanced and Readable (walimwuliza)
decisions.reason: Luke tells this past event in the present (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable use the narrative past.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὅπου τὸ σῶμα, ἐκεῖ καὶ οἱ ἀετοὶ ἐπισυναχθήσονται.

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, Where the body [is], there also the vultures will be gathered together.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Where the body [is], there also the vultures will be gathered together."
en.B: He said to them, "Where the corpse lies, there the vultures will flock together."
en.R: Jesus answered, "The vultures come together wherever the dead body is."

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les dijo: «Donde [esté] el cuerpo, allí también se juntarán los buitres».
es.B: Él les dijo: «Donde esté el cadáver, allí se juntarán los buitres».
es.R: Jesús les respondió: «Los buitres se juntan dondequiera que haya un cuerpo muerto».

sw.L: Naye akawaambia, "Mahali [ulipo] mwili, huko pia tai watakusanyika pamoja."
sw.B: Akawaambia, "Mahali maiti ilipo, tai watakusanyika huko kwa wingi."
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Tai hukusanyika popote palipo na mwili uliokufa."

decisions.choice: where the body is, the vultures gather: a proverb meaning it will be plain to see and cannot be escaped
alternatives: a statement about where the judgment will take place on a map
decisions.reason: Birds circling in the sky show from far off where a dead animal lies. Jesus does not name a place; when the time comes, it will be as plain as that, and judgment will come where it is due (compare Matthew 24:28).

decisions.choice: vultures: birds that feed on dead bodies
decisions.reason: The word can mean eagle or vulture. Birds gathering at a dead body are vultures.

decisions.choice: body: here a dead body
decisions.reason: The word means body; with the birds it means a dead one.

decisions.choice: corpse (B); dead body (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear the body is dead.

decisions.choice: los buitres
decisions.reason: The Greek word can name eagles, but birds that gather at a dead body are vultures (meaning decision m2), as in Matthew 24:28.

decisions.choice: tai
decisions.reason: The birds that gather at a dead body are vultures (meaning decision m2). "Tai" names both vultures and eagles, as the Greek word can, as in Matthew 24:28.
